findings.mechanism: Both carrier termination branches are unpopulated, leaving zero populated resistive termination conductance on the carrier. Complete-bus termination therefore depends on circuitry outside the reviewed carrier.
findings.reasoning: The schematic, exported connectivity and saved board agree on this omission. Termination adequacy and resulting communication behavior cannot be established because brain-module termination, harness topology and bit rate are unspecified. Static ERC and zero unconnected PCB items do not resolve that uncertainty.
findings.title: CAN2 termination depends on unspecified module or harness circuitry

findings.mechanism: ERC reports three undriven power-input declarations, an unhandled A1 fault-output connection, and two interconnected J2 sensor-supply pins both typed as power outputs.
findings.reasoning: The five native errors reproduce independently despite exit status zero. This is a schematic declaration defect; the evidence does not establish absent physical power, a regulator collision, or a requirement to monitor the unused fault output.

limitations: No bench measurements or validated functional simulations; supplied checks contain no electrical stimulus or waveform measurements.
Manufacturer-reference retrieval failed because DNS was unavailable; independent device pinout, threshold and rating validation remains incomplete.

Brain-module internals, harness termination, firmware reset states, startup, shutdown and brownout behavior were not established. LS9/LS10 divider calculations alone did not establish a threshold violation.

Automotive transients, ignition energy, motor loads, wideband stability, EMC and thermal qualification remain omitted. Copper was evaluated as saved without refill; DRC records were inspected rather than rerun.

Integrated FOME-MC coverage, manufacturing approval and the original as-received filename discrepancy are outside this review. Commands, versions, assumptions and outcomes are recorded in review-work/circuit/experiments/review-notes.md.
